questions.question:
**Direction: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.**

(A) that further treatment

(B) useless

(C) the doctor concluded

(D) would be
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "CADB."** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence follows the subject-verb-Object (SVO) structure.
 
• **"The doctor"** is the subject, and** "concluded" **is the verb. So the first part must be C.
 
• **"That further treatment"** is the first part of the object. So, it must be A.
 
• The phrase **"that further treatment"** serves as a subordinating conjunction, connecting the doctor's conclusion to the statement about uselessness.
 
• The word **"useless"** is an adjective modifying the noun** "treatment." **So the last part must be the pair** DB.**
 
• The correct answer is option 1.

 

**Correct sentence**: *The doctor concluded that further treatment would be useless.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The bell is rung by the peon.

options.text: The peon has rang the bell.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"The peon rings the bell."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in Passive Voice and Simple Present tense. 
 
• As per the given question, we have to change it into Active Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject (objective case)+ is/am/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
• Subject + V1(s/es)+ Object. (Active Voice)
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Their cousin show them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They are shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'bell' and the object is 'peon.' 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• 'Is rung' will be changed into 'rings.' 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2.'

Correct sentence: *The peon rings the bell.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

It is __**nothing**__ but pride.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "nothing else."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Nothing else"** is a suitable substitute for **"nothing"** in the given sentence.
 
• This phrase means that there is nothing in addition to pride, emphasizing the singular focus on that emotion.
 
• The use of **"else"** implies that there are other possibilities, but in this case, there are none.
 
• The sentence structure is grammatically correct, with **"nothing"** being the subject and** "else"** serving as an adverb modifying it.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, "nothing ever," **does not convey the same meaning as the original sentence, as it implies a sense of time rather than exclusivity.
 
• **Option 3, "nothing seldom," **is a grammatically incorrect phrase, as "seldom" is an adverb and cannot be used to modify "nothing."
 
• **Option 4, "nothing so," **is also grammatically incorrect, as "so" requires a comparison to something else (e.g. "nothing so beautiful as a sunset").

• Part D introduces the **subject + verb "The theater management recommends" **to the sentence. So, this must be the first part.
 
• The next part is the pair EB as it introduces the relative clause with **"****that the audience should be there."**
 
• The next part is the object of the sentence, i.e. the pair CA.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.
 
• **Correct sentence**: 

 

*The theater management recommends (D) that the audience (E) should be there (B) at least fifteen minutes (C) before the movie starts (A).*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Ramya laughed at me.

options.text: I am laughed at by Ramya.
I were laugh at by Ramya.
I was laughed at by Ramya.
I shall laugh at by Ramya.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "I was laughed at by Ramya."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **Active Voice.** As per the given question we have to change it into **Passive Voice. **
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• **Subject + V2 + Object. (Active Voice)**
 
• **Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)**
 
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. **(Active Voice)***
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. **(Passive Voice)***
 
 
 
• **The subject** of the given sentence is **'Ramya.'​​**
 
• **The object** of the given sentence is** 'me.' **
 
• **The subject** will be put in place of** the object **and** the object **will be put in place of **the subject.**
 
• 'Laughed' will be changed into **'was laughed'. **
 
• **"I" **is a singular subject and we must use **"was"** with it.
 
• The preposition "by" is used to indicate the doer of the action in the passive voice.
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 ​

**Correct sentence**: *I was laughed at by Ramya.*
